modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 1 > ProfDev > Design Practice and Scrum Understanding
modules.title: Design Practice and Scrum Understanding
modules.focus: This module focuses on strengthening visual design practice through Illustrator and understanding structured teamwork through Scrum.
modules.whatIDid: I created Illustrator exercises such as a name combination graphic and a Christmas card, and I studied Scrum roles including Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developer.
modules.keyResult: The result was a small set of design practice outputs together with a clearer understanding of how Scrum supports team-based work.
modules.whatILearned: I learned that Illustrator is useful for precise visual work such as logos, icons, posters, and other creative assets, and that Scrum helps teams through clear roles, sprint goals, and risk management.
modules.reflection: This module works best as a compact starting point that introduces both creative practice and structured collaboration.
modules.playHook: A simple design-completion puzzle or a Scrum-role matching interaction would fit this module well.
modules.outcomeDescription: Illustrator exercises and visual design practice results.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 2 > ProfDev > Proto Website Redesign
modules.title: Proto Website Redesign
modules.focus: This module focuses on redesigning the Proto website to improve usability while practicing UX and UI thinking and reflective design work.
modules.whatIDid: I analyzed the existing website, identified navigation pain points, proposed a Quick Access button, sketched ideas on paper, built Figma mockups, and refined them through committee feedback.
modules.keyResult: The main outcome was a set of Figma redesigns that communicated a clearer and more professional website direction, even though the implementation phase was delayed.
modules.whatILearned: I learned to balance creativity with practical usability, to keep design tools like Figma actively practiced, and to use iteration and feedback to improve decisions.
modules.reflection: I was proud of the design progress, but missed meetings, holidays, exams, and the lack of user data made the process slower and showed that better timeline buffers were needed.
modules.playHook: A UI rearrangement puzzle where the player fixes broken layout sections or selects the best usability improvements would match this module well.
modules.outcomeDescription: Proto website redesign mockups and UI improvement results.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 3 > ProfDev > BuildCV Idea Proposal
modules.title: BuildCV Idea Proposal
modules.focus: This module focuses on entrepreneurship proposal writing and developing a vague idea into a structured concept.
modules.whatIDid: I reviewed around 20 ideas, selected a CV platform concept, researched competitors and market trends, named it BuildCV, designed a logo, and used personas, SWOT, competitor analysis, and 4P strategy to strengthen the proposal.
modules.keyResult: The final result was a usable proposal for BuildCV with strategic framing, visual elements, and a development timeline.
modules.whatILearned: I learned how to write more professionally in English, organize an idea through strategic tools, and transform short rough notes into a much stronger document.
modules.reflection: Changing the challenge was frustrating at first, but it led to a more complete and useful result; the biggest lesson was that project scope must fit collaborators’ pace and deadline reality.
modules.playHook: A timed pitch-building game, keyword-combination challenge, or strategy-card matching mini game would connect naturally to this module.
modules.outcomeDescription: BuildCV proposal visuals, logo, and concept summary.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 4 > ProfDev > Rebuilding Portfolio Website with React
modules.title: Rebuilding Portfolio Website with React
modules.focus: This module is about rebuilding an old portfolio into a more modern, maintainable, and industry-aligned website using React.
modules.whatIDid: I replaced the old portfolio because it felt too plain, buggy, and difficult to maintain, researched references, collected feedback, and rebuilt the portfolio using React and Tailwind.
modules.keyResult: The outcome was a new portfolio with a cleaner layout, stronger technical structure, and a more professional presentation than the previous version.
modules.whatILearned: I learned React and Tailwind CSS, understood the importance of user testing for UX, and improved my time management through planning and iteration.
modules.reflection: I felt the new version looked clean and intuitive with strong performance, but language switching and mobile optimization still needed work.
modules.playHook: A reconstruction puzzle where portfolio blocks must be placed into the correct layout would reflect this module clearly.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 5 > ProfDev > Upgrading Rascal Cat for Release
modules.title: Upgrading Rascal Cat for Release
modules.focus: This module focuses on improving a game jam prototype into a more polished and publishable game with better systems and presentation.
modules.whatIDid: I reviewed player feedback, listed launch tasks, improved gameplay balance, added more objects, managed systems with GameManager, integrated a PlayFab leaderboard, and prepared and published the game on itch.io.
modules.keyResult: The result was a published downloadable version of Rascal Cat supported by improved systems, leaderboard integration, screenshots, and release material.
modules.whatILearned: I learned more about the full game development lifecycle, external service integration, polishing through feedback, and the practical side of publishing a game online.
modules.reflection: The project became much more complete and real, but WebGL support problems in the newer Unity version blocked browser play and showed I needed earlier platform research.
modules.playHook: A bug-catching game or a balancing mini game inspired by Rascal Cat’s stacking chaos would fit perfectly here.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 6 > ProfDev > Learning Python through Advent of Code
modules.title: Learning Python through Advent of Code
modules.focus: This module is about building coding confidence by learning Python through real problem-solving instead of only grammar study.
modules.whatIDid: I started from job-posting analysis, chose Python because it felt the least familiar yet useful, and used Advent of Code as a daily problem-based learning structure.
modules.keyResult: The result was Advent of Code progress, related GitHub work, and a clearer understanding of what technical foundations I still need.
modules.whatILearned: I learned that solving real problems is more motivating than isolated syntax study, and that Python basics alone are not enough without stronger algorithm knowledge.
modules.reflection: The challenge became much harder than expected, which shifted my goal from finishing everything to learning more deeply and realistically.
modules.playHook: A logic puzzle, code-order arrangement task, or simplified Advent-of-Code-style question would represent this module well.
modules.outcomeDescription: Advent of Code progress and coding result snapshot.

modules.path: TwenteUni > CreaTe > Module 7 > ProfDev > CV, Portfolio, and Job Market Preparation
modules.title: CV, Portfolio, and Job Market Preparation
modules.focus: This module focuses on preparing for internships and jobs by refining a usable CV, redesigning the portfolio, and gaining real networking experience at the Business Fair.
modules.whatIDid: I collected content from previous CVs, tried building a new CV in Overleaf, brought it to the Business Fair for feedback, spoke with 17 companies over 2 days, revised the CV in Figma, redesigned project detail pages in Notion, updated the portfolio’s hero and skill and tool sections, and migrated deployment from GitHub Pages to Vercel.
modules.keyResult: The result was a finalized CV, an improved portfolio with stronger project pages, a more flexible deployment setup, real applications sent to 3 companies, and a September internship interview already scheduled.
modules.whatILearned: I learned how external feedback changes CV clarity, how portfolio structure affects self-presentation, how networking gives practical information about applications, and how experimenting with Overleaf, Figma, Notion, and Vercel expanded my workflow.
modules.reflection: I was proud that I completed almost everything on time and turned both the CV and portfolio into practical application tools, but I still wanted more feedback through a CV workshop and saw backend or admin tooling as the next improvement area.
modules.playHook: A CV-building or recruiter-match mini game, where the player chooses and arranges the right experience for a target company, matches this module very well.
modules.outcomeDescription: Final portfolio website and application-ready outcome.
